sections.content: You know these four time frames from earlier units: the pretérito perfecto (Unit 1), the pretérito indefinido (Unit 11), ir a + infinitive (A1) and the futuro simple (Unit 19). Here they work together. Use the *pretérito perfecto* for recent experiences connected to the present, the *pretérito indefinido* for completed events, *ir a* + infinitive for immediate plans and the *futuro simple* for predictions and longer-term goals. Familiar connectors and comparatives can help link the ideas.

items.spanish: Hemos aprendido mucho desde aquel día.
items.english: We have learnt a lot since that day.

items.spanish: Van a empezar un nuevo capítulo.
items.english: They are going to begin a new chapter.
The world will be their classroom.

sections.content: *Hemos aprendido* looks back to what we have done, *caminaron* tells what happened, and *van a empezar* and *será* look forward.
